metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–15% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility and overconfidence — dampen forecast variance and anchor to recent 7-day moving average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast exceeds 20% above recent 14-day high, reduce by 10–20%.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a forecast peak, model should adjust downward by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to avoid lagged overreaction.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model should not extrapolate beyond 10% above or below recent 18-day range — use tighter bounds to avoid overfitting.
